title: Scheme Analysis
description: Preserves how an offensive or defensive system works, what personnel it requires and how it changes fantasy-relevant roles.
principles: Describe the mechanism, not only a scheme label.
Separate scheme from coach identity when the source does.
Link affected roles and players without reducing the scheme take to one player.
Preserve fit, misfit, transition and uncertainty.

dimensions.description: Named or described system, concepts and structural characteristics.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain the defining concepts in source-supported language.
detection_questions: What does the scheme actually do?

dimensions.description: How the scheme creates or removes opportunities.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Explain the causal path to snaps, touches, targets, efficiency or scoring.
detection_questions: What mechanism matters for fantasy outcomes?

dimensions.description: Archetypes, personnel groups and role requirements.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the traits and roles the system needs.
detection_questions: Which player types fit or struggle?

dimensions.description: How responsibilities are divided within a unit.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain role specialization, concentration or rotation.
detection_questions: How are carries, routes, targets or blocking responsibilities distributed?

dimensions.description: Expected effect on volume and efficiency.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep volume and efficiency claims separate.
detection_questions: Does the scheme create more opportunity, better efficiency or both?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve why an entity fits or fails to fit.
detection_questions: Which players or positions benefit and why?

dimensions.description: Situations where the expected effect may fail.
detection_questions: What roster, quarterback, line or game-state condition could break the thesis?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Does the extraction explain how the scheme works rather than naming it?
Are volume and efficiency effects distinguished?
Are affected roles and personnel requirements preserved?
Is a structural scheme take independently reusable?
forbidden_distortions: Do not use a scheme label as a substitute for reasoning.
Do not guarantee production from scheme fit.
Do not merge coach history and current scheme without source support.
Do not invent technical football detail absent from the source.
extension_signals: A recurring scheme mechanism is not represented.
The source introduces a new personnel or role framework.
The existing subject types cannot express a system or unit concept.
A scheme discussion requires a new Golden Set reference.
